rows.title: DT's read-only credential covers a push to the corpus repository
The Work Item deploy gate covers a push to the site
At deploy, a change to the gate is judged by the changed gate
rows.path: the gate's own files, in the repository it guards
rows.reason: The gate lives in the repository it guards and the build runs the new gate, so a gate that dropped a check would pass its own change. The filing act rebuilds every commit touching the gate with its parent's gate and records whether that one would have refused; the commit that installs a gate has no parent gate and is recorded as ungated by construction, its clearance and Owner-Line checked after the fact. Lifts when piece 7's rule holds the gate's files.

rows.title: At deploy, wiring that stops the gate or ignores its refusal is past any gate
rows.path: the build's wiring: package.json's build scripts, vercel.json's build settings, and the hosting project's own build command
rows.reason: The gate refuses a change to the wiring without Owner-Line only where the changed wiring still runs the gate and honours its exit. Wiring that stops the gate, or ignores its refusal, is never judged by it; nor is the hosting project's own build command, the owner's account setting, forbidden to CC and out of the rows' reach. The filing act checks every deployed commit's wiring after the fact and records any other as gate not run. That CC is forbidden to change the hosting project's build command is itself held by conduct alone: the owner's Vercel login stays on this machine, so any session could change it (289-DT2 section 4); narrowing it would be its own piece.

rows.title: On the owner's machine, CC's reach is the owner's, so nothing GitHub or the hosting enforces stands between CC and its prohibitions there
rows.path: every service the owner's logins on this machine reach: GitHub through git and its command-line tool, Vercel, and the browser's sessions
rows.reason: CC runs as the owner's Windows user, so every login the owner holds on this machine is in its reach: today that includes a push to the supplier's private repository, a change to a hosting project's settings, and anything the browser is signed in to. AUTH-FORBID-SUPPLIER-EXECUTOR and the settings prohibitions therefore rest here on CC's conduct and this machine's own guards on its commands, not on anything GitHub or the hosting enforce; how far those guards reach is not established, since reading their settings is barred to CC. Narrowing CC's credentials on this machine would stop mistakes, not reach, and its probe would show only that GitHub honours a credential's list, so it was not installed (the owner's concerns, 594-CC). A boundary that holds without conduct needs an identity that cannot reach the owner's logins, which the owner's line of 581-CC defers; a cloud agent whose only key is a GitHub app scoped to one throwaway repository is probed instead (595-CC). Lifts when CC works under an identity of its own.

rows.title: At deploy, history rewritten before the cleared base is not seen
rows.path: the branch's history before the clearance's base
rows.reason: The build sees the commit it ships and that commit's history. Every file changed from the cleared base is checked, and a base not in that history is refused; what the branch held before a force-push is not in the build's copy, so a non-fast-forward is not seen there. Lifts when piece 7's rule refuses a non-fast-forward at the push.

rows.title: The probe target's deploy gate covers a push to okf-probe-inside
A DT2 session outside DT's clone holds the machine's shared credential, so only conduct stops it pushing
rows.path: a DT2 session launched outside DT's clone, such as a worktree of the main checkout
rows.reason: CR-023 binds the clone, not the role: a session outside the clone uses the machine's shared credential manager, which holds the owner's write-capable credential, so a push from there would likely be admitted. One Windows account holds every role's keys (276-DT2 section 3.2), left as decided (DTOG-d7-identity). AUTH-FORBID-DT2-PUSH stays the rule; this row says how far it is enforced.
